pairs.subject: copy-quality-gates
pairs.evidence: app/admin/AdminGate.tsx:40 The /admin gate renders literal Czech copy in JSX that sits outside the copy gate's only declared source (messages/en.json), and the gate's report neither extracts it nor declares it out of scope, so a green copy-check says nothing about this surface.

techniques.evidence: app/admin/AdminGate.tsx:40 Rule: copy outside the catalog is extracted through the same pipeline or declared out of scope in the report. The contract lists only messages/en.json with exclude: [], and report.mjs:17 prints only strings checked, so these literals are an undeclared source. The opt-out exists only as a code comment (app/admin/page.tsx:8), and the 'boundary note in features/admin/' it points to was not found by search.

app/admin/loopActions.ts:74 L1 includes no literal user-visible string escaping the catalog. This server-action error is a hardcoded literal that reaches the operator via setLastError(res.error) at features/admin/components/LoopMissionControl.tsx:140, and no configured check sees it. The checker can extract jsx and ts-module kinds, but the contract does not enable them.

app/data/page.tsx:11 The signal needs target failures in at least two languages per source unit. These routes have one source (cs) and one target (en), confirmed by locales at lib/i18n/config.ts:8, so it cannot fire.

pairs.registryProposal: The standard gives no explicit treatment for an operator-only, single-locale internal console. rendered-string-extraction allows declaring such copy out of scope in the report, while layered-mechanical-gate L1 lists literals escaping the catalog with no scope exception, and copy-contract-before-drafting exempts only a one-off internal string. A decision rule on whether a whole non-localized operator surface may be declared out of L1 would remove this ambiguity.
